verses.text: When the people saw that Moses was taking a long time to come down from the mountain, they gathered around Aaron and said, "Come, make us gods who will lead us. As for this Moses who brought us up out of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him."
Aaron answered them, "Take off the gold earrings that your wives, your sons, and your daughters are wearing, and bring them to me."
So all the people took off their gold earrings and brought them to Aaron.
He took what they gave him and shaped it with a tool into a statue of a calf. Then they said, "Israel, these are your gods, who brought you up out of Egypt!"
When Aaron saw this, he built an altar in front of the calf and announced, "Tomorrow there will be a feast to the LORD."
So the next day the people got up early and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. Afterwards they sat down to eat and drink, and then got up to party wildly.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go down, because your people, whom you brought up out of Egypt, have become wicked.

They have quickly turned away from what I commanded them. They have made themselves a statue of a calf. They have bowed down to it and offered sacrifices to it, and they have said, 'Israel, these are your gods, who brought you up out of Egypt.'"
The LORD said to Moses, "I have seen these people, and they are stubborn people.
Now leave me alone, so that my anger can burn against them and I can destroy them. Then I will make you into a great nation."
But Moses begged the LORD his God. He said, "LORD, why should your anger burn against your people, whom you brought out of Egypt with great power and a mighty hand?

Why should the Egyptians say, 'He brought them out to do them harm, to kill them in the mountains and wipe them off the face of the earth'? Turn from your fierce anger. Change your mind, and do not bring this disaster on your people.

Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. You made a promise to them, swearing by your own name: 'I will make your descendants as many as the stars in the sky. I will give your descendants all this land I promised them, and it will be theirs forever.'"
So the LORD changed his mind and did not bring on his people the disaster he had spoken of.
Moses turned and went down the mountain with the two tablets of the covenant in his hands. They were written on both sides, front and back.
The tablets were the work of God. The writing was the writing of God, carved on the tablets.
When Joshua heard the noise of the people shouting, he said to Moses, "There is the sound of war in the camp."
Moses replied, "It is not the sound of people shouting because they have won, and it is not the sound of people crying because they have lost. It is the sound of singing that I hear."
When Moses came near the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, his anger burned. He threw the tablets out of his hands and broke them to pieces at the foot of the mountain.
He took the calf they had made and burned it in the fire. Then he ground it into powder, scattered it on the water, and made the people of Israel drink it.
Moses said to Aaron, "What did these people do to you, that you led them into such a great sin?"
Aaron answered, "Do not be angry, my lord. You know how these people are set on doing evil.
They said to me, 'Make us gods who will lead us. As for this Moses who brought us up out of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.'
So I told them, 'Whoever has any gold, take it off.' They gave me the gold, and I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf!"
Moses saw that the people were out of control. Aaron had let them get out of control, so that they became a joke to their enemies.
So Moses stood at the entrance to the camp and said, "Whoever is on the LORD's side, come to me!" And all the Levites gathered around him.

Then he said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Each man must strap a sword to his side. Go back and forth through the camp from one end to the other, and each of you kill his brother, his friend, and his neighbour.'"
The Levites did what Moses commanded, and about three thousand of the people died that day.
Then Moses said, "Today you have set yourselves apart for the LORD, because each of you was against his own son and brother. So he has given you a blessing today."
The next day Moses said to the people, "You have committed a terrible sin. But now I will go up to the LORD. Maybe I can make peace with him for your sin."
So Moses went back to the LORD and said, "Oh, these people have committed a terrible sin. They have made themselves gods of gold.
But now, please forgive their sin. If you will not, then wipe my name out of the book you have written."
The LORD answered Moses, "Whoever has sinned against me, I will wipe his name out of my book.
Now go and lead the people to the place I told you about. My angel will go ahead of you. But when the time comes for me to punish them, I will punish them for their sin."
And the LORD sent a plague on the people because of what they did with the calf Aaron had made.
